text:
ashwin_r: Heads-up — sampleapp upload flow is spamming duplicate POSTs after a 401 -> token refresh on Android 15 emulator. Happens reliably if network toggles during refresh. Repro steps + logs below.

jia_liu: ugh. do you have a minimal repro or the stack trace?

ashwin_r: yes, minimal repro in the sampleapp (UploadActivity). Steps: 1) sign in, 2) start upload, 3) force token expiry on server, 4) flip airplane mode for ~1s then back. Observed: client sends original POST, gets 401, starts refresh, then two POSTs land after refresh. Logs: 

```
2026-03-20 14:02:11.123 D/OkHttp: --> POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/upload
2026-03-20 14:02:11.456 D/OkHttp: <-- 401 https://api.redwood.ai/v1/upload (60ms)
2026-03-20 14:02:11.457 D/Auth: starting refresh token request
2026-03-20 14:02:11.800 D/Network: airplane mode toggled
2026-03-20 14:02:12.050 D/OkHttp: --> POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/upload (replay?)
2026-03-20 14:02:12.050 D/OkHttp: --> POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/upload (again)
```

ashwin_r: Client setup is Retrofit + Kotlin suspend CallAdapter (already using `suspend` services) and an OkHttp Authenticator that performs the refresh via blocking network call. OkHttp client config: `retryOnConnectionFailure(true)`, `dispatcher.maxRequestsPerHost = 5` (default).

sam_k: couple of thoughts: 1) Authenticator runs on the response path and its contract can cause the same request to be retried transparently; 2) coroutine call adapters + cancellation/resume can end up recreating calls if not careful. Are you using `suspend fun upload(...)` with an interceptor that re-enqueues?

ashwin_r: yes `suspend fun upload(file: MultipartBody.Part): Response<Unit>`; we aren't manually re-enqueuing. I suspect the combination of network toggling + authenticator + dispatcher leads to duplicate creation.

jia_liu: can you paste the authenticator code? Also what's the behavior if you set `retryOnConnectionFailure(false)`?

ashwin_r: authenticator snippet:

```
class TokenAuthenticator : Authenticator {
  override fun authenticate(route: Route?, response: Response): Request? {
    synchronized(this) {
      val newToken = tokenProvider.refreshTokenBlocking()
      return response.request.newBuilder()
        .header("Authorization", "Bearer $newToken")
        .build()
    }
  }
}
```

ashwin_r: Setting `retryOnConnectionFailure(false)` reduces duplicates but doesn't eliminate them; still see occasional doubles.

sam_k: ok. unique angle: the Kotlin coroutine adapter will cancel and recreate the underlying Call if the coroutine is resumed on a different dispatcher or timed out, which can combine with Authenticator transparently retrying the call. Two in-flight call objects can result if the first isn't marked canceled before authenticator completes. Workaround: make the refresh logic idempotent and guard replays with an in-process refresh lock at the HTTP-client level.

jia_liu: can you try switching to an Interceptor-based refresh that uses a single shared suspend-safe refresh token flow? Example pattern: have an AtomicReference<Deferred<String>?> that stores the in-flight refresh so concurrent request threads wait on the same deferred instead of issuing multiple refreshes. Also avoid blocking network calls inside `Authenticator` (it runs on OkHttp internal threads).

ashwin_r: thanks — will try an interceptor approach. quick prototype we used: 

```
// inside Interceptor
val token = currentToken()
val req = chain.request().newBuilder().header("Authorization", "Bearer $token").build()
val resp = chain.proceed(req)
if (resp.code == 401) {
  val refresh = refreshState.getOrPut { asyncRefreshToken() } // pseudo
  val newToken = runBlocking { refresh.await() }
  return chain.proceed(req.newBuilder().header("Authorization", "Bearer $newToken").build())
}
return resp
```

ashwin_r: using this, duplicates dropped to near zero in my local stress test. main downside: having blocking `runBlocking` in interceptor felt gross but it's isolated and keeps us off OkHttp internal authenticator flow.

sam_k: instead of runBlocking, you can integrate with `suspendCancellableCoroutine` in a custom CallAdapter that exposes suspension to the interceptor, but that's heavier. For stability, keep the refresh single-flight using e.g. `CompletableDeferred` + `synchronized`/`AtomicReference`. Also set `dispatcher.executorService().shutdown()`? nah that's unrelated.

devex-bot: Created ticket RED-IO-4219 with repro and suggested Interceptor single-flight pattern. Patch candidate attached to the issue. <https://redwood.internal/issue/RED-IO-4219>

jia_liu: filing internal sampleapp PR would be great — add a comment about Android 15 network toggles and the coroutine adapter caveat. Add an e2e test that toggles connectivity during refresh.

ashwin_r: will open PR today. thanks for the pointers :thumbsup:

sam_k: short-term: document `retryOnConnectionFailure` interactions and recommend interceptor single-flight refresh in onboarding guide. Long-term: consider adding a helper `TokenRefreshInterceptor` to the SDK that is coroutine-friendly and prevents duplicate downstream calls.

ashwin_r: agreed — I'll include the helper in the PR so other engs can reuse it.
